spec_text:
Notes app. People sign up with a username (3-32 letters, digits or underscore) and a password of at least 8 characters,
then log in to get a token. Wrong passwords are rejected, and after 5 failed logins in a minute the account is locked out
for a while. Logged-in users can create notes with a title (1-100 chars) and an optional body (up to 10000 chars).
They can list their notes, search by title, and page through them (default 20, max 100 per page). They can read, edit
and delete a note by id. Each user must only ever see and change their own notes, never anyone else's. Everything except
signup, login and the health check needs a valid token. Errors must not expose internals like stack traces. The service
exposes GET /health returning 200 when it is running and ships in a Docker container.

test_r6_list_search_paging
examples.code:
# reqs: R6
# hint: listing, searching or paging notes is wrong
import os
import uuid

import httpx

BASE = os.environ["BASE_URL"]


def client():
    return httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=10)


def new_user(cl, password="password123"):
    name = "u" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]
    assert cl.post("/auth/signup", json={"username": name, "password": password}).status_code == 201
    token = cl.post("/auth/login", json={"username": name, "password": password}).json()["token"]
    return name, {"Authorization": "Bearer " + token}


def add_note(cl, auth, title="t", body="b"):
    r = cl.post("/notes", json={"title": title, "body": body}, headers=auth)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    return r.json()["id"]

def test_list_returns_only_own_notes_in_order():
    with client() as cl:
        _, auth = new_user(cl)
        ids = [add_note(cl, auth, title=f"note{i}") for i in range(3)]
        assert [n["id"] for n in cl.get("/notes", headers=auth).json()] == ids


def test_search_by_title():
    with client() as cl:
        _, auth = new_user(cl)
        add_note(cl, auth, title="groceries")
        add_note(cl, auth, title="work")
        assert [n["title"] for n in cl.get("/notes", params={"q": "groc"}, headers=auth).json()] == ["groceries"]


def test_paging_defaults_and_limits():
    with client() as cl:
        _, auth = new_user(cl)
        for i in range(25):
            add_note(cl, auth, title=f"n{i}")
        assert len(cl.get("/notes", headers=auth).json()) == 20
        assert len(cl.get("/notes", params={"limit": 100}, headers=auth).json()) == 25
        assert cl.get("/notes", params={"limit": 101}, headers=auth).status_code == 422
        assert cl.get("/notes", params={"limit": 0}, headers=auth).status_code == 422
        assert cl.get("/notes", params={"offset": -1}, headers=auth).status_code == 422
        assert len(cl.get("/notes", params={"limit": 10, "offset": 20}, headers=auth).json()) == 5
        assert len(cl.get("/notes", params={"limit": 1}, headers=auth).json()) == 1

examples.code:
# reqs: R7
# hint: reading, editing or deleting a note by id is wrong
import os
import uuid

import httpx

BASE = os.environ["BASE_URL"]


def client():
    return httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=10)


def new_user(cl, password="password123"):
    name = "u" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]
    assert cl.post("/auth/signup", json={"username": name, "password": password}).status_code == 201
    token = cl.post("/auth/login", json={"username": name, "password": password}).json()["token"]
    return name, {"Authorization": "Bearer " + token}


def add_note(cl, auth, title="t", body="b"):
    r = cl.post("/notes", json={"title": title, "body": body}, headers=auth)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    return r.json()["id"]

def test_read_update_delete_roundtrip():
    with client() as cl:
        _, auth = new_user(cl)
        nid = add_note(cl, auth, title="a", body="b")
        assert cl.get(f"/notes/{nid}", headers=auth).json() == {"id": nid, "title": "a", "body": "b"}
        up = cl.put(f"/notes/{nid}", json={"title": "a2", "body": "b2"}, headers=auth)
        assert up.status_code == 200 and up.json()["title"] == "a2"
        assert cl.get(f"/notes/{nid}", headers=auth).json()["body"] == "b2"
        assert cl.delete(f"/notes/{nid}", headers=auth).status_code == 204
        assert cl.get(f"/notes/{nid}", headers=auth).status_code == 404


def test_update_validates_input_and_missing_note_is_404():
    with client() as cl:
        _, auth = new_user(cl)
        nid = add_note(cl, auth)
        assert cl.put(f"/notes/{nid}", json={"title": "", "body": ""}, headers=auth).status_code == 422
        assert cl.put("/notes/999999999", json={"title": "t", "body": ""}, headers=auth).status_code == 404
        assert cl.delete("/notes/999999999", headers=auth).status_code == 404

examples.code:
# reqs: R9
# hint: some endpoints work without a valid token
import os
import uuid

import httpx

BASE = os.environ["BASE_URL"]


def client():
    return httpx.Client(base_url=BASE, timeout=10)


def new_user(cl, password="password123"):
    name = "u" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]
    assert cl.post("/auth/signup", json={"username": name, "password": password}).status_code == 201
    token = cl.post("/auth/login", json={"username": name, "password": password}).json()["token"]
    return name, {"Authorization": "Bearer " + token}


def add_note(cl, auth, title="t", body="b"):
    r = cl.post("/notes", json={"title": title, "body": body}, headers=auth)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    return r.json()["id"]

def test_protected_routes_reject_missing_or_bad_tokens():
    with client() as cl:
        _, auth = new_user(cl)
        nid = add_note(cl, auth)
        for bad in ({}, {"Authorization": "Bearer nope"}, {"Authorization": "Basic abc"}, {"Authorization": "Bearer x"}):
            assert cl.get("/notes", headers=bad).status_code == 401
            assert cl.post("/notes", json={"title": "t", "body": ""}, headers=bad).status_code == 401
            assert cl.get(f"/notes/{nid}", headers=bad).status_code == 401
            assert cl.put(f"/notes/{nid}", json={"title": "t", "body": ""}, headers=bad).status_code == 401
            assert cl.delete(f"/notes/{nid}", headers=bad).status_code == 401


def test_public_routes_need_no_token():
    with client() as cl:
        assert cl.get("/health").status_code == 200
